summary: Backend and platform software engineer (6+ years, Python) who builds systems that keep themselves running: self-healing automation, distributed storage, asyncio services, PostgreSQL, CI/CD. Sets the engineering standards, reviews the code and mentors engineers across a ~12-engineer department; outside work, builds Terraform-managed platforms on Google Cloud and AWS.

bullets: Escalation point and code-review gate for a ~12-engineer department automating HughesNet's satellite gateways: review ~10 pull requests a week across every repository, own merges to main, and have mentored and onboarded 5 engineers

Defined the department's engineering standards and built the tooling behind them: introduced continuous integration (Jenkins) with a dev-to-main review flow, PostgreSQL and Grafana; designed the shared logging entry point used by every script and device module; standardized email and Teams alerting, and the master tables every alert and self-heal writes to

Authored the platform's Kubernetes migration design covering 161 scheduled jobs and made the shared library cluster-ready (stdout log collection, service-DNS database routing, unit-tested), on a Patroni-managed high-availability PostgreSQL pair

Root-caused and eliminated a platform-wide logging defect that silently discarded log records, cutting the log footprint from 19.68 GB to 58 MB and reclaiming ~25 GB in production; swept all 146 scheduled jobs for the same pattern

Root-caused two production failures: a 738 MB core dump traced with gdb to an unguarded deserialization path in a vendor gateway component, and a 177-process leak traced to a library deadlock at interpreter teardown; delivered both as actionable defect reports and shipped the supervision module that closed the leak
Lead analyst on infrastructure failure investigations, on call 24/7 against a 99.9% SLA; rollback owner in change control
Automated software validation and hardware testing across 20+ ATM models with PowerShell and Python scripts
Built a Jenkins CI/CD framework that standardized releases, moved builds from weekly to hourly and cut setup time 15%

systems.name: Sightline
bullets: Led the 6-person team behind a lunar landing-site planner (NASA Space Apps 2026): assigned work, reviewed pull requests, owned the architecture and built all the Google Cloud infrastructure, directing AI coding agents that wrote most of the code. Python pipeline on NASA SPICE/LOLA data matches JPL Horizons within 0.0071° over 5,469,984 hourly checks. Four Cloud Run services behind a load balancer, CDN and Cloud Armor, all in Terraform applied from GitHub Actions with no stored keys; canary deploys with automatic rollback; 2,020 tests in CI

systems.name: Ceph Storage Self-Healing Monitor
bullets: Replaced a manual on-call recovery that took ~1.5 hours per storage failure, an outage for 40,000–60,000 subscribers about every two weeks on the newest satellite system, with automated failover inside one 3-minute cycle, across 24 storage nodes in 8 clusters. Failover gated by a four-verdict standby-capacity assessment so it never moves into a worse node, outcomes verified against the cluster log to distinguish a real failover from a same-node reclaim. Sole author (6,586 lines, 61 tests)

systems.name: Config Integrity Self-Heal
bullets: Closed an outage path that cut off 20,000–30,000 subscribers about once a month, when a modem failover landed on drifted configuration: detects drift across 18 gateways at 8 sites over SFTP and restarts the affected service, with 89% of episodes closing inside one 10-minute polling cycle. Modernized a blocking-I/O workload onto asyncio with semaphore-bounded fan-out rather than process pools. Sole author (3,594 lines, 76 tests)
